name: Trickster
flavor: Every illusion is misdirection with better staging. You cut out the staging.

features.name: Two Places at Once
features.description: When you use Misdirection to move after casting a trick, you can spend 1 Phantasm to leave a silent, motionless illusory double of yourself standing in the space you left. Until the start of your next turn, the first attack roll made against you is made with **disadvantage** — the attacker commits to the wrong one of you before it can tell which is breathing. The double then vanishes, whether or not anyone swung at it. It is only ever an image: it has no space of its own that matters, it cannot be attacked, and nobody ever has to work out which of the two of you they are targeting.
features.sheetSummary: Leave a motionless illusory double in the space Misdirection moved you out of: the FIRST attack roll against you before the start of your next turn is made with disadvantage, then the double vanishes. No targeting choice for anyone to make.
features.narration: You step away and something stays — the same coat, the same posture, holding perfectly still where you were a moment ago. Whoever swings next has to decide, in the time it takes to swing, and they get it wrong.

features.name: Palmed
features.description: Hide the real work inside the loud work: once on each of your turns, when you cast a Turn, you may also cast one Pledge as part of the same action. The Pledge resolves after the Turn. With Palmed Card in your list this is a second attack every round for nothing, which is the whole reason to take this discipline.
features.sheetSummary: When you cast a Turn, also cast one Pledge as part of the same action; the Pledge resolves after the Turn.
features.narration: The big gesture is the cover. The small one, the one that actually matters, happens inside it while everyone is busy applauding the wrong hand.

features.name: Second Nature
features.description: Sleight of hand has stopped requiring your attention. You can palm, plant, swap, or produce any object small enough to fit in one hand without being noticed, with no check, provided nobody is deliberately watching your hands. Against a creature that IS watching your hands, you have advantage on the check. You can also perform any Pledge without any visible gesture at all, so nobody can tell you cast anything.
features.sheetSummary: Palm, plant, swap, or produce a hand-sized object with no check. A creature deliberately watching your hands makes it a Sleight of Hand check at advantage instead. You can cast any Pledge with no visible somatic component.
features.narration: The hands do it without being asked any more. You have handed back a stolen ring while apologising for the theft and nobody in the room, including the owner, saw either half.
